extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, industry stakeholders, public commenters, attorneys, and researchers who track DOT Federal Register actions
extracted.subtask_description: A machine-readable listing (API JSON) of U.S. Department of Transportation Federal Register documents (rules, notices, proposed rules, ADs, funding opportunities, information-collection notices, SORNs, etc.), with metadata and short abstracts intended to support public notice-and-comment and stakeholder monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — solicitation of public comments for information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: "In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following collection of information was published on January 20, 2026."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the PRA procedural requirement: agencies must publish notices inviting public comment when seeking OMB approval or renewal of information collections, typically giving a specified comment period (example: 60 days). The notice should identify the collection, its purpose, and cite the PRA as authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum required fields for voluntary information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: "The required fields in the Noise Portal represent the minimum information necessary for the FAA to respond effectively."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing an information collection (even voluntary), identify the required fields and justify that they represent the minimum information necessary for the agency to perform its functions (responding to complaints, preventing fragmented responses, etc.). Explain benefits such as transparency, centralized intake, and community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA new collection notices — statement of use/purpose and user benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: For the FAA Surface Weather Status Dashboard collection: "The information to be collected will be used to verify and track these errors and outages, and publish the status onto the FAA's Surface Weather Status Dashboard for user awareness."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New-collection notices must state how collected information will be used, what problems it addresses (e.g., verify/track outages), and the public benefit (user awareness, improved operations).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA justification of continuing need and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Bureau of Transportation Statistics invites the general public, industry and other governmental parties to comment on the continuing need for and usefulness of DOT requiring U.S. and foreign air carriers to file traffic and capacity data pursuant to 14 CFR 241.19 and Part 217, respectively."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices asking for renewal must solicit comment on whether the information collection remains necessary and useful, and evaluate burden vs. benefit; they should cite the regulatory citations that require the filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-permit notices — solicitation of comments and evaluation role
rubrics_metrics.description: "PHMSA is publishing this notice to solicit public comments on a request for a special permit... Argent LNG is seeking relief from compliance with certain requirements in the Federal pipeline safety regulations. PHMSA has proposed conditions to ensure that the special permit is consistent with pipeline safety. At the conclusion of the 30-day comment period, PHMSA will review the comments received from this notice as part of its evaluation to grant or deny the special permit request."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special-permit notices must summarize the request, identify proposed conditions to protect safety, set a public-comment period (example: 30 days), and state that comments will be reviewed and considered in the grant/deny decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airworthiness directive content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: "This AD requires an operational check of the pitch trim actuator... an option to do a pitch trim verification, and applicable on-condition actions." and "requires, for certain airplanes, doing a 'local thickness mapping,' doing applicable additional instructions, a general visual inspection (GVI) of certain forward fuselage panels, a full panel thickness measurement, and applicable corrective actions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADs must (a) identify the unsafe condition prompting the AD, (b) specify required actions (inspections, operational checks, measurements), (c) provide on-condition/corrective actions and allowable compliance options if applicable, and (d) explain the safety rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airspace amendment justification tied to NAVAID changes
rubrics_metrics.description: "The FAA is taking this action due to the planned decommissioning of the VOR portion of the Pullman, MI, VOR/Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) navigational aid (NAVAID). This NAVAID is being decommissioned as part of the FAA's VOR Minimum Operational Network (MON) program."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to amend, establish, or revoke airspace must explain the technical justification (e.g., NAVAID decommissioning, MON program) and how route/network continuity or safety will be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airspace legal-description administrative revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: "This action ... makes several administrative revisions to TRM's legal descriptions reflecting information from the FAA's aeronautical database."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When updating airspace regulations, agencies should update legal descriptions to match authoritative aeronautical databases and describe administrative corrections separately from substantive airspace changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction amendments to final rules for non-substantive errors
rubrics_metrics.description: "That final rule contained typographical, grammatical, and formatting errors in three sections of Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations. This document corrects those errors in the final regulations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may issue correction amendments to fix typographical/formatting/grammatical errors in codified regulations; such corrections should be identified and limited to non-substantive fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act system-of-records notice (SORN) content
rubrics_metrics.description: "In accordance with the Privacy Act of 1974, the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), proposes a new system of records titled 'DOT/ FMCSA 015 FMCSA Registration Records.' The purpose of this system of records is to allow FMCSA to consolidate the existing FMCSA registration systems..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SORN notices must provide the system name, purpose, statutory authority, scope/contents (what records are included), and the rationale for consolidation or new system creation, consistent with the Privacy Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive funding opportunity notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Federal Transit Administration (FTA) announces the opportunity to apply for $28,492,618 million in competitive grants for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Pilot Program for Transit-Oriented Development Planning."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding opportunity notices should clearly state the administering agency, program name, fiscal year, total available funding amount, and that they announce an opportunity to apply; further details (eligibility, application process, deadlines) appear in the full notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices announcing committee/public meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: "This notice announces a public meeting of the Technical Pipeline Safety Standards Committee, also known as the Gas Pipeline Advisory Committee (GPAC), to discuss the notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM)..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting notices must identify the committee, meeting purpose/topics, and link to the NPRM or subject matter; they provide an opportunity for stakeholders to attend and submit input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions of inconsequential noncompliance — receipt and summary
rubrics_metrics.description: "Kawasaki Motors Corp., U.S.A. ... has determined that certain model year ... motorcycles do not fully comply with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 122... Kawasaki filed a noncompliance report ... and subsequently petitioned NHTSA ... for a decision that the subject noncompliance is inconsequential as it relates to motor vehicle safety. This document announces receipt of Kawasaki's petition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies publish notices when they receive petitions asserting that a regulatory noncompliance is inconsequential, summarizing the noncompliance, the petition, the standard at issue, and providing opportunity for public comment or agency action.
